([[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]]) * [[McEachern High School|McEachern]]
([[Powder Springs, Georgia]]) | college = [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] (2020–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team2 = →[[Stockton Kings]] | highlights = }} '''Dylan Cardwell''' (born December 16, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. ==Early life and high school== Cardwell attended [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] up to his junior season before transferring to [[McEachern High School]] for his senior year. As a junior he averaged 3.8 points and 3.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last=Vitale |first=Josh |title=3-star center Dylan Cardwell commits, gives Auburn much-needed big man |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2020/05/07/three-star-center-dylan-cardwell-commits-auburn-basketball-gives-bruce-pearl-top-recruiting-class/3090455001/ |website=Montgomery Advisor |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=May 7, 2020}} Coming out of high school, Cardwell was rated as a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]] over other schools such as Georgia, Tennessee, Miami, Maryland and UConn.{{cite web |last=Green |first=Tom |title=3-star center Dylan Cardwell commits to Auburn |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2020/05/3-star-center-dylan-cardwell-commits-to-auburn.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=May 7, 2020}} ==College career== As a [[freshman]] in 2020–21, Cardwell appeared in 27 games where he averaged 3.8 points and 3.6 rebounds in 15.2 minutes per game.{{cite web |last=Bharucha |first=Manush |title=Who Is Dylan Cardwell? Everything You Need to Know About Auburn’s 6′ 11″ Center |url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/ncaa-college-basketball-news-who-is-dylan-cardwell-everything-you-need-to-know-about-auburn-s-six-eleven-center/ |website=Essentially Sports |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=December 23, 2024}} On January 11, 2022, he tallied six points, six rebounds and four blocks in a win over rival [[2021–22 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]].{{cite web |last=Green |first=Tom |title=Dylan Cardwell turns heel vs. Alabama, finishes as Auburn’s ‘most important player’ in win |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2022/01/dylan-cardwell-turns-heel-vs-alabama-finishes-as-auburns-most-important-player-in-win.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=January 12, 2022}} During the 2021–22 season, Cardwell appeared in all 34 games and averaged three points and three rebounds.{{cite web |last=Green |first=Tom |title=Auburn’s Dylan Cardwell withdrawing from NBA Draft, returning for 2022-23 season |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2022/05/auburns-dylan-cardwell-withdrawing-from-nba-draft-returning-for-2022-23-season.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=May 31, 2022}} In the first two games of the 2022–23 season, he put up nine points and ten blocks.{{cite web |last=Green |first=Tom |title=Dylan Cardwell’s rim protection a ‘factor’ for No. 13 Auburn early this season |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2022/11/dylan-cardwells-rim-protection-a-factor-for-no-13-auburn-early-this-season.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=November 15, 2022}} In the 2022–23 season, Cardwell averaged 3.7 points and 3.8 rebounds in 32 appearances.{{cite web |last=Silva |first=Richard |title=Dylan Cardwell, three other Auburn basketball players listed as early entrants for draft |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2023/04/25/dylan-cardwell-auburn-basketball-2023-nba-draft-early-entry-candidate-jaylin-williams-johni-broome/70140810007/ |website=Montgomery Advisor |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=April 25, 2023}} In 2023–24, he averaged 5.3 points, 1.6 blocks and 1.2 assists in 14.7 minutes per game.{{cite web |last=Noyes |first=Craig |title=Dylan Cardwell announces return to Auburn for 5th season |url=https://www.theplainsman.com/article/2024/04/dylan-cardwell-announces-return-to-auburn-for-5th-season |website=The Auburn Plainsman |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=April 11, 2024}} Heading into the 2024–25 season, Cardwell become a full-time starter for the first time.{{cite web |last=Rauterkus |first=Peter |title=How Dylan Cardwell’s decision to ‘fight, not flee,’ etched his name in Auburn history |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2025/02/how-dylan-cardwells-decision-to-fight-not-flee-etched-his-name-in-auburn-history.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=February 28, 2025}} On December 30, 2024, he posted 12 points, 11 rebounds, two blocks and a steal in a win over [[2024–25 Monmouth Hawks men's basketball team|Monmouth]].{{cite web |last=Locke |first=Daniel |title=Auburn's Dylan Cardwell 'Grateful' for Breakout Performance |url=https://www.si.com/college/auburn/basketball/auburn-dylan-cardwell-grateful-breakout-performance-01jgme65jgt2 |work=SI.com |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=January 2, 2025}} On March 1, 2025, Cardwell become the all-time winningest player in Auburn men’s basketball history, with 115 wins after he helped the Tigers to a 94–78 win over [[2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]].{{cite web |last=Rauterkus |first=Peter |title=Dylan Cardwell becomes all-time winningest player in Auburn men’s basketball history |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2025/03/dylan-cardwell-becomes-all-time-winningest-player-in-auburn-mens-basketball-history.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 7, 2025|date=March 1, 2025}} ==Professional career== On June 26, 2025 after being undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Cardwell signed a [[Two-way contract|two-way contract]] with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web |last=Zimmerle |first=Will |title=Kings Sign 6-Foot-11 Center After 2025 NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/nba/kings/sacramento-kings-news/breaking-kings-sign-6-foot-11-center-after-2025-nba-draft-01jyqpacv3jw |website=si.com |access-date=June 29, 2025|date=June 27, 2025}} On February 6, 2026, the Kings signed Cardwell to a four-year, $8.3 million standard contract after trading [[Dennis Schröder|Dennis Schroder]], [[Keon Ellis]] and [[Dario Šarić]] as part of a three-team deal that brought [[De'Andre Hunter]] to Sacramento. At the time of the signing, Cardwell was leading his rookie class in blocks per game,{{Cite web |title=Sacramento Kings Sign Dylan Cardwell |url=https://kings.com/news/sacramento-kings-sign-dylan-cardwell |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=kings.com |language=en|date=2025-02-05}} and he led all rookies in rebounds per game in the same month. Cardwell recorded a career-high 15 points against the Los Angeles Clippers on April 5th, 2025, alongside four blocks. == Career statistics == {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player
